content: The prevalence of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) among individuals with type 2 diabetes is approximately 23%. Furthermore, up to 58% of these individuals experience some form of sleep-disordered breathing. In individuals with obesity who participated in the Look AHEAD trial, the prevalence of OSA was even higher, exceeding 80%. People who exhibit symptoms of OSA, such as excessive daytime sleepiness, loud snoring, or observed episodes of apnea during sleep, should undergo appropriate screening for the condition. However, the evidence regarding the direct impact of sleep apnea treatment on glycemic control remains inconclusive.
